answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a nontrivial stake in a vault before it may vote on trades or claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits prove coordinated fraud. The stake is returned after a clean review period, so creating many accounts ties up capital for each one; spreading a saffron-and-pearl marketplace across fresh names no longer makes influence cheap. An attacker must risk real funds and keep them locked, while honest newcomers can build reputation gradually.
